name: Enoch
overview: Enoch was a male figure uniquely identified as the son of Cain, according to Genesis 4:17. There is no record of his tribe or additional notes, making his primary distinction his lineage from Cain. This positions him early in the biblical genealogies following the fall of man.
namesAndTitles: The name Enoch means 'initiated' or 'follower,' reflecting a possible characteristic or role attributed to him. This proper name is recorded in Genesis 4:17 and was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Enoch as the son of Cain and the father of Irad, establishing a direct father-son lineage in the early generations after Adam. No other family relationships are documented beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Enoch's significance lies primarily in his place within the early genealogical record as a descendant of Cain. While other biblical figures named Enoch have notable spiritual roles, this particular Enoch is distinguished by his lineage and contribution to the early human population. His mention in Scripture helps trace the development of humanity following the fall, underscoring God's ongoing providence in human history.

keyEvents.event: Taken by God (did not see death)
